record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Reversible entanglement manipulation under PPT operations
record.original_question: For bipartite entanglement manipulation in the asymptotic limit, local operations and classical communication are irreversible for mixed states, while more general positive-partial-transpose-preserving operations might restore reversibility. Are PPT-preserving operations sufficient for asymptotically reversible interconversion of all pure and mixed bipartite entangled states? If so or if not, what is the smallest nontrivial operation class that permits such asymptotically reversible interconversion for all bipartite entangled states?

evidence.quote: Asymptotic reversibility under a class of operations would lead to a unique entanglement measure and impose a unique ordering on entangled states thereby playing a role similar to entropy in thermodynamics.

The following are open questions:
• Are ppt-operations sufficient to ensure asymptotically reversibly interconversion of all, i.e. pure and mixed, bi-partite entangled states [BFC]?
• What is the smallest non-trivial class of operations that permits asymptotically reversibly interconversion of all, i.e. pure and mixed, bi-partite entangled states [Bet]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bipartite quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces H_A ⊗ H_B and the set of quantum states (density operators) on them. A quantum operation Λ from bipartite states on H_A ⊗ H_B to bipartite states on H_{A'} ⊗ H_{B'} is called PPT-preserving if it is completely positive, trace-preserving, and the map (T_{B'} ∘ Λ ∘ T_B) is also completely positive, where T_X denotes partial transposition on system X; equivalently, Λ maps every state with positive partial transpose to a state with positive partial transpose.

Given a class C of bipartite operations and two bipartite states ρ and σ, define the asymptotic transformation rate R_C(ρ → σ) as the supremum of r ≥ 0 such that there exists a sequence of operations Λ_n ∈ C with Λ_n(ρ^{⊗ n}) → σ^{⊗ ⌊rn⌋} in trace norm as n → ∞. The pair (ρ, σ) is said to be asymptotically reversibly interconvertible under C if R_C(ρ → σ) · R_C(σ → ρ) = 1.

(a) Is the class of PPT-preserving operations sufficient to ensure that every pair of bipartite entangled states (pure or mixed) on arbitrary finite-dimensional bipartite systems is asymptotically reversibly interconvertible, in the sense that for any two entangled states ρ, σ one has R_PPT(ρ → σ) · R_PPT(σ → ρ) = 1?

(b) If the answer to (a) is negative, determine the smallest (in the sense of inclusion, or some natural physically motivated minimality criterion) nontrivial class of bipartite operations under which every pair of bipartite entangled states (pure and mixed) is asymptotically reversibly interconvertible.
artifact.status_search_result: Part (a) has been resolved negatively: it was shown that asymptotic entanglement manipulation under operations completely preserving the positivity of partial transpose is irreversible in general, so PPT-preserving operations are not sufficient for reversible interconversion of all bipartite entangled states. Part (b), identifying the smallest nontrivial class of operations allowing universal asymptotic reversibility, remains open; subsequent work has explored larger classes (e.g., operations beyond completely positive maps) and identified specific mixed states (such as antisymmetric Werner states) where PPT reversibility does hold.

status_evidence.title: Irreversibility of Asymptotic Entanglement Manipulation Under Quantum Operations Completely Preserving Positivity of Partial Transpose
status_evidence.snippet: Irreversibility of asymptotic entanglement manipulation under quantum operations completely preserving positivity of partial transpose is demonstrated.
status_evidence.claim: PPT-preserving operations are not sufficient for asymptotic reversibility of all bipartite entangled states.

status_evidence.claim: The general problem of identifying the minimal class of operations giving universal asymptotic reversibility is tracked as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Reversible entanglement beyond quantum operations
status_evidence.snippet: Work exploring reversible entanglement manipulation beyond standard quantum operations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work investigates broader operation classes to recover asymptotic reversibility, indicating the minimal-class question remains active.
